speakers.name: Nikoleta Kouli
speakers.session: Opening: Chikuzen Hakata Koma
speakers.bio: Nikoleta is a community leader, writer, and podcast host who moved from chemical engineering into community building. Her work in coliving focuses on helping people find connection and a sense of belonging.

speakers.name: Akina Shu
speakers.bio: Akina founded Nomad University and co-founded Colive Fukuoka. A digital nomad since 2019, she draws on conversations with nomads around the world to create media and programs that connect people across cultures.
speakers.session: Co-founders Opening Talk

speakers.name: Ryo Osera
speakers.bio: Ryo is the CEO of yugyo inc. and founder and producer of Colive Fukuoka. He co-founded the travel-subscription service HafH and previously worked at Dentsu and as Social Media Director for the Japanese Prime Minister’s Office. His work connects global talent with communities in Japan.
speakers.session: Co-founders Opening Talk

speakers.name: Masaomi Sakata
speakers.session: Gut-Health Breakfast: Elevating IQ and Happiness through Gut Health
speakers.bio: Masaomi, also known as Koji Prince, develops foods and sweets using fermentation. He launched the 15% brand to make food more inclusive, beginning with an ice cream project that grew from his own exploration of food and well-being.

speakers.name: Chikushi Shuraku III
speakers.session: Opening: Chikuzen Hakata Koma
speakers.bio: Chikushi Shuraku III is the twentieth-generation head of Chikuzen Hakata Koma, a traditional spinning-top performance recognized as an intangible cultural property of Fukuoka Prefecture. He also performs Hakata Kinshishi taiko and brings these traditions to audiences in Japan and overseas.

speakers.name: Yumi Imamura (matchabae)
speakers.session: Keynote 2: Matcha Crisis
speakers.bio: Yumi grew up in a tea-selling family and shares Japanese tea culture with audiences in Japan and overseas. She leads Chajiyuukan, offering tea experiences through a mobile tea room that brings tea, time, and place together.

speakers.name: Kiki Fukai
speakers.session: Become Yourself Here: Japan as the Place You Discover Who You Really Are
speakers.bio: Kiki is a personal branding coach and content creator. Having lived abroad and worked alongside international residents in Japan, she brings perspectives from both sides of cross-cultural life. She helps people find their own voice and build a sense of belonging without losing who they are.

speakers.name: Ryotaro Sakurai
speakers.session: YEN TO EN: Turning Money Back into Connection
speakers.bio: Ryotaro founded Life Bridge in 2006. He works with local governments and tourism businesses on inbound tourism, regional development, and travel experiences. Through Ryotaro’s Japan, he introduces places and people across Japan to English-speaking audiences.

speakers.name: Kazuhiro Arai
speakers.session: YEN TO EN: Turning Money Back into Connection
speakers.bio: Kazuhiro co-founded Kamakura Investment Management in 2008 and established eumo in 2018. Following a career in banking and investment management, he explores economic models built around empathy, human connection, and well-being.

speakers.name: Kotaro Motojima
speakers.session: YEN TO EN: Turning Money Back into Connection
speakers.bio: Kotaro is a lawyer whose work has included DAO development and legal frameworks with the Japan DAO Association and RuleMakers DAO. At IVS2024, he discussed how legal structures can support communities working toward shared goals.

speakers.name: Kiyoko Mitsui
speakers.session: YEN TO EN: Turning Money Back into Connection
speakers.bio: Kiyoko leads the KIBOTCHA Smart Eco-Village initiative in Higashimatsushima. Her work connects disaster-prevention education, the reuse of a former school, and community development, exploring ways for people to learn and build a sustainable future together.

speakers.name: Mikiko & Hidehiko Sudo
speakers.session: Wakachiai: From Everyday Talk to Deep Connection
speakers.bio: Mikiko and Hidehiko are relationship specialists, educators, and founders of Kokoro Academy. Mikiko brings a background in university teaching and communication; Hidehiko holds a PhD in Sport Science and works with behavior change. Together, they developed Wakachiai, a practical approach to sharing feelings and building trust.

speakers.name: Sanae Akima
speakers.session: Beneath Ikigai & Zen: Discovering the Hidden Worldview of Japan, and Your Own
speakers.bio: Sanae is a practitioner-researcher and founder of La torche. She develops projects that help people and communities turn differences into new possibilities. These include Nashite Fukuoka, a community and media initiative exploring why people from different backgrounds are drawn to the city. She is also the author of Brain Management.

speakers.name: Miki Tsukamoto (Visions)
speakers.session: Rain Won't Stop You, Wind Won't Stop You: Live Music, Picture Books and Miyazawa Kenji in Two Languages
speakers.bio: Miki is a pianist and co-founder of Visions with bassist and percussionist Kiyoshi Mamura. Formed in 2000, the duo uses jazz improvisation as a foundation for collaborations with picture-book readings, film, theater, dance, and traditional performing arts.

speakers.name: Kiyoshi Mamura (Visions)
speakers.session: Rain Won't Stop You, Wind Won't Stop You: Live Music, Picture Books and Miyazawa Kenji in Two Languages
speakers.bio: Kiyoshi is a bassist and percussionist who formed Visions with pianist Miki Tsukamoto in 2000. Their work combines jazz improvisation with other art forms, including storytelling, film, theater, dance, and traditional performance.

speakers.name: Multilingual Matt
speakers.session: Speak Before You're Ready
speakers.bio: Matt creates content about language learning, travel, culture, and cross-cultural connection. His work combines humor, storytelling, and practical advice, treating language as a way to practice courage and humility while connecting with people across borders.

speakers.name: Gil Petersil
speakers.session: ChaTea Workshop
speakers.bio: Gil is a facilitator, speaker, and co-founder of ChaTea. His work centers on human communication and relationship building through intentional networking, tea ceremonies, and shared experiences. He helps groups create trust and turn new connections into collaboration.

speakers.name: Stella Schneider
speakers.session: SME Takeover Lab [ATOTSUGI]: How to Acquire a Small Business
speakers.bio: Stella is a German business strategist and founder of Business Wege. She helps founders and entrepreneurs choose business models suited to their goals, from freelancing and small businesses to acquiring an existing company. Her work connects personal priorities with practical business decisions.

speakers.name: Daycia
speakers.session: Content Strategy for Small Businesses
speakers.bio: Daycia created Daylightful, a media brand focused on human connection, intentional travel, and slow cultural immersion. Previously, she worked on content and campaign strategy at Dentsu and P&G. She now shares practical content strategies with small-business owners.

speakers.name: Yarden Avirav & Roza Gavrilov
speakers.session: Breaking Conceptions: From Nomadic Couple to Nomadic Family
speakers.bio: Yarden and Roza are the couple behind NomadsTwoGo. After years of living and working as digital nomads, becoming parents in 2025 changed how they think about travel, freedom, and home. They share their ongoing experience of finding a nomadic lifestyle that works for a family.

speakers.name: Nika Rey
speakers.session: Latino Dance: Bachata for Everyone
speakers.bio: Nika is an international dance instructor and event organizer who encourages people to move, connect, and enjoy music through dance.

speakers.name: Diego Taira
speakers.session: Build Wealth. Find Your Purpose. Design a Life You Don't Need to Retire From.
speakers.bio: Diego is the co-founder and CEO of Wealth Angels.

speakers.name: Roland Tokko
speakers.session: Align and Connect with Your Ikigai Through Soul
speakers.bio: Roland is an Estonian speaker, facilitator, and singer-songwriter, and co-founder of Becoming International. He combines speaking, live music, singing, and guided experiences to help people explore purpose and leadership in their own lives.

speakers.name: Adam Curnow
speakers.session: Travel Smarter, Work Safer: Everyday Security for Digital Nomads
speakers.bio: Adam founded KarasuSec and works in IT and cybersecurity. A digital nomad himself, he focuses on making security understandable and practical for people who work from anywhere.

speakers.name: Oren Chazan
speakers.session: Peace: One Conversation at a Time
speakers.bio: Oren co-owns Montino Coliving and works as an advertising consultant and business coach. Trained in Nonviolent Communication and related practices, he creates coliving and conversation experiences that encourage connection, community, and a more peaceful way of living.

speakers.name: Yeji Cheon
speakers.session: Peace: One Conversation at a Time
speakers.bio: Yeji founded Seoul Nooks, an intentional coliving and coworking community. Her work connects local Asian cultures with global nomad communities, using workshops and conversations to explore cultural differences, diversity, and how people live together.

speakers.name: Cihan Boz
speakers.session: Peace: One Conversation at a Time

speakers.name: Carlyn Shaw
speakers.session: The Power of a Smile: Creating Connection and Joy Within and Around You
speakers.bio: Carlyn is a speaker, writer, and creator of the Whoever Smiles First Wins movement and Live In Joy community. Through travel and everyday encounters, she encourages people to trust themselves, build connections, and make room for joy.

speakers.name: Tressia H. Lee
speakers.session: HEARIM: Building Trust Across Cultures at Work
speakers.bio: Tressia is a global marketing and Korean cultural strategist from Seoul. She created HEARIM, a Korean-informed communication framework for understanding unspoken expectations and building trust across cultures. Her background spans marketing, localization, education, and cultural strategy, alongside a remote-working career that began in 2014.

speakers.name: Lawrence Tuazon
speakers.session: Beyond Social Media: Grow a Business Through Relationships, Trust and Community
speakers.bio: Lawrence is an author, speaker, coach, and co-founder of Be Extraordinary Publishing. He helps people turn their experiences into meaningful work and grow businesses through relationships, partnerships, referrals, and community.

speakers.name: Gen Lee
speakers.session: Anywhere, But Where?
speakers.bio: Gen founded LocalNomad and explores the future of work, play, and belonging in legacy cities.

speakers.name: Marco Traina
speakers.session: What Keeps a Community Alive? From Shared Spaces to Shared Purpose
speakers.bio: Marco is an entrepreneur and community builder who founded BeetCommunity in Palermo and Italia Nomad Fest. He also co-founded COFO – Coliving Founders. His work connects remote workers and local residents, encouraging visitors to participate in local life and contribute to the communities that host them.

speakers.name: Freeman Fung
speakers.session: A Conscious Pause: Closing Meditation at the Water's Edge
speakers.bio: Freeman is a speaker, author, mindset coach, and meditation facilitator. He founded Travel To Transform and combines personal development with travel and conscious global citizenship. His work encourages people to cultivate presence, self-understanding, and meaningful connections.

speakers.name: Arthur Binard
speakers.session: Rain Won't Stop You, Wind Won't Stop You: Live Music, Picture Books and Miyazawa Kenji in Two Languages
speakers.bio: Arthur is an American-born poet and translator who began writing poetry in Japanese after moving to Japan in 1990. His work spans poetry, essays, picture books, and kamishibai storytelling, including translations between Japanese and English.

speakers.name: Nick Szasz (FUKUOKA NOW)
speakers.session: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
speakers.bio: Nick founded Fukuoka Now in 1998. Through English-language publishing, he introduces Fukuoka and Kyushu to international readers and helps connect visitors and residents with local places, people, and culture.

speakers.name: Douglas Weber
speakers.session: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
speakers.bio: Douglas is a designer and engineer who studied at Stanford and worked on product design at Apple. At Weber Workshops, he brings that experience to the design and engineering of coffee equipment.

speakers.name: Jean-Pierre Villeneuve
speakers.session: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
speakers.role: Founder and CEO, New Town Technologies
speakers.bio: Jean-Pierre is the founder and CEO of New Town Technologies, the company behind the Seratone karaoke system.

speakers.name: Micaela Anne
speakers.session: Keynote 1: Why We Came, Why We Stayed, and What Comes Next
speakers.bio: Micaela is a Canadian-born creator who calls Fukuoka home. Through Fukuoka Eats, she shares local food, travel, and everyday discoveries from the region.

speakers.name: Ukiha no Takara
speakers.session: Gut-Health Breakfast: Elevating IQ and Happiness through Gut Health
speakers.bio: Ukiha no Takara is a social enterprise in Ukiha, Fukuoka. Its Grandma’s Café initiative creates meaningful paid work for older women, allowing them to share a lifetime of cooking skills, local recipes, hospitality, and wisdom. The team brings generations together through food, community, and a sense of purpose. At the Academy breakfast, the grandmothers share handmade onigiri and Japanese home cooking.
speakers.members: Two members of Grandma’s Café and Okuma Mitsuru
speakers.group_image_alt: Ukiha no Takara on stage at Colive Fukuoka

speakers.name: Jacquie Wortley
speakers.session: Where can we build something that matters?
speakers.bio: Jacquie draws on a decade of UX and product research in her work on sustainable innovation. Working with rural tea farmers, she explores how projects can support local people and regenerate the places they depend on.

speakers.name: Ryu Fujii
speakers.session: Where can we build something that matters?
speakers.bio: Ryu co-founded 369meteor and co-organizes ZōVillage. He is involved with Fracton Ventures and Network School, connecting experimental global communities with grassroots initiatives.

speakers.name: MOE Nakano (JDNA)
speakers.session: Ask a Digital Nomad: Open Roundtables with JDNA
speakers.role: Representative Director, Japan Digital Nomad Association
speakers.bio: Moe, also known as Tomoe Nakano, moved from design into community building through Asia’s coworking movement. She founded TAOHUB in Thailand, TANEHUB in Akita, and the Japan Digital Nomad Association, where she leads the Community Manager Academy.

speakers.name: Vitto Christaldi (JDNA)
speakers.session: Ask a Digital Nomad: Open Roundtables with JDNA
speakers.bio: Vitto is a coworking and community strategist whose experience includes Hubud, Dojo, Tribal, and BWork. His work brings people together through shared workplaces and community experiences, including CU Asia.

speakers.name: Tessei Hosokawa
speakers.session: The "Death" of Digital Nomads — Zen, Impermanence, and Living in the Moment
speakers.bio: Tessei is a Kyoto-based entrepreneur and founder of NEWSON&COMPANY and Immersive Lab. Early monastic training at a Sōtō Zen temple continues to inform his work. He founded TABICA, now aini, and works across community building, regional revitalization, and immersive experiences.

speakers.name: Akira Iguchi
speakers.session: IKIGAI MANIFESTATION: How to Turn Your Ikigai into an Extraordinary Life — The 5-Step Formula to Live the Life You Truly Want
speakers.bio: Akira is an entrepreneur, author, speaker, and founder of Human Plus Inc. His work brings together entrepreneurship, personal development, and his Ikigai Manifestation Method to help people connect their strengths with meaningful work and purpose.

speakers.name: Jessica Hagmaier
speakers.bio: Jessica is a creative strategist, brand designer, and travel writer. Through long-term solo travel, she explores reinvention, personal freedom, and intentional living, combining storytelling with practical approaches to navigating change.
speakers.session: You Can't Outrun Your Life: How to Use Travel as a Catalyst for Reinvention
